# 30-Day Guitar Rhythm Plan

A simple 20-minutes-a-day plan to turn 3 basic chords into steady timing and 2 playable songs. It focuses on rhythm first, then chord changes, then full-song run-throughs.

## Month Plan at a Glance

| Week | Main goal | Rhythm focus | Song focus | End-of-week win |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Lock in steady strumming | Count in 4/4, downstrokes, metronome at slow tempo | Learn Song 1 chords and one easy strumming pattern | Play 1 chord loop without stopping |
| 2 | Clean chord changes with time | Down-up strums, accent on beat 2 and 4 | Finish Song 1 sections and start Song 2 chords | Play Song 1 at slow tempo |
| 3 | Build full-song stamina | Muting, lighter strums, switching patterns smoothly | Finish Song 2 parts and connect song sections | Play both songs in chunks |
| 4 | Perform both songs | Tempo control, consistent groove, no stopping | Full-song run-throughs and simple performance practice | Record both songs from start to finish |

## Weekly Rhythm Goals

### Week 1: Steady Beat
- Count aloud: “1 2 3 4” while strumming.
- Use only downstrokes at first.
- Practice 2-chord and 3-chord loops with no rushing.
- Target tempo: **60 bpm**.

### Week 2: Add Flow
- Switch to down-up strumming.
- Keep your strumming hand moving even when changing chords.
- Accent beats **2** and **4**.
- Target tempo: **65–70 bpm**.

### Week 3: Make It Musical
- Use softer strums on verses and stronger strums on choruses.
- Practice stopping cleanly on the last beat of a section.
- Work on smooth transitions between song parts.
- Target tempo: **70–80 bpm**.

### Week 4: Play Through
- Run each song without stopping.
- Fix only the biggest timing problems.
- Practice beginning, middle, and ending sections separately, then together.
- Target tempo: **song speed if comfortable, otherwise 80% speed**.

## Daily 20-Minute Practice

### Daily structure
- **3 min** — Warm-up: finger stretch + open-string strums
- **5 min** — Rhythm drill: clap or strum with metronome
- **5 min** — Chord change practice
- **5 min** — Song work
- **2 min** — Quick review and note your progress

### Day-by-day plan

| Day | Focus | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Baseline | Set your metronome, strum one chord for 4 beats, notice where you rush |
| 2 | Counting | Count “1 2 3 4” out loud while strumming downstrokes |
| 3 | Chord loop | Switch between 2 chords slowly, staying on beat |
| 4 | Simple pattern | Try down-down-down-down, then down-up once if comfortable |
| 5 | Song 1 intro | Learn the first verse or main chord loop of Song 1 |
| 6 | Timing check | Play chord changes with metronome at a slow speed |
| 7 | Review day | Repeat the hardest exercise from the week and record 1 minute |

| Day | Focus | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | Down-up strumming | Practice a steady down-up motion on one chord |
| 9 | Beat accents | Strum a little stronger on beats 2 and 4 |
| 10 | Song 1 verse | Play the verse slowly and keep the rhythm even |
| 11 | Song 1 chorus | Learn the chorus or next section |
| 12 | Chord changes | Repeat the 3 hardest chord changes from Song 1 |
| 13 | Song 2 intro | Learn the first chord loop of Song 2 |
| 14 | Review day | Play Song 1 sections back-to-back without stopping |

| Day | Focus | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| 15 | Groove control | Practice softer strums, then louder strums on the same chord loop |
| 16 | Clean stops | Stop on beat 4 and restart on beat 1 |
| 17 | Song 1 full run | Play Song 1 slowly from start to finish |
| 18 | Song 2 verse | Learn the verse or main repeating section |
| 19 | Song 2 chorus | Add the chorus or second section |
| 20 | Transition practice | Move between verse and chorus without losing count |
| 21 | Review day | Record both songs in short sections |

| Day | Focus | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| 22 | Tempo stability | Play the same progression 3 times without speeding up |
| 23 | Song 1 polish | Fix the weakest chord change or rhythm spot |
| 24 | Song 2 polish | Fix the weakest chord change or rhythm spot |
| 25 | Full Song 1 | Play Song 1 through with metronome or backing track |
| 26 | Full Song 2 | Play Song 2 through with metronome or backing track |
| 27 | Performance practice | Stand up and play both songs like a mini performance |
| 28 | Review day | Revisit the toughest section of each song |

| Day | Focus | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| 29 | Final polish | Play both songs once slowly, once at your best comfortable tempo |
| 30 | Final recording | Record both songs start to finish and compare to Day 1 |

## Two-Song Learning Path

Pick songs with:
- 3 to 4 easy chords
- A repeating strumming pattern
- A slow or medium tempo
- Clear verse/chorus sections

Good song types for this plan:
- Acoustic pop songs with simple chord loops
- Folk songs with steady down-up strumming
- Beginner rock songs with 3 or 4 open chords

If you already have songs in mind, use this rule:
- **Song 1** = easier song for confidence
- **Song 2** = slightly harder song to stretch your rhythm

## Simple Progress Tracker

Use this quick score after each practice session:

| Item | Score 0–2 | What it means |
|---|---|---|
| Timing | 0 = off beat, 1 = mostly steady, 2 = steady throughout |
| Chord changes | 0 = many stops, 1 = some clean changes, 2 = smooth changes |
| Song sections | 0 = not learned, 1 = partial, 2 = complete |
| Confidence | 0 = frustrated, 1 = okay, 2 = comfortable |

### Daily log
- Date:
- Minutes practiced:
- Metronome tempo:
- Song practiced:
- Timing score:
- Chord score:
- One thing that improved:
- One thing to fix tomorrow:

### Weekly check
- Can I keep a steady beat for 1 minute?
- Can I switch chords without losing the count?
- Can I play Song 1 from start to finish?
- Can I play Song 2 from start to finish?
